findings.observation: The enabled orange primary buttons use white text at approximately 3.74:1 contrast, below 4.5:1 for their small bold labels.
findings.impact: The central review and confirmation actions are harder to read.
findings.repair: Darken the orange until white labels reach 4.5:1; recheck both enabled actions in the selected and review captures.

findings.observation: The selected 10:30 slot changes fill and border color but has no checkmark or explicit selected label. The selected service does have a checkmark.
findings.impact: Time selection is less explicit than service selection and relies on color treatment to communicate state.
findings.repair: Add a persistent checkmark or selected label to the chosen time, retaining its time text. Recheck the narrow two-column time grid.

strengths: Service names, prices, dates and times support a clear choose–review–confirm sequence.
The review state makes the selected service, price and time easy to inspect, with a clearly subordinate change action.
Confirmation explicitly says nothing was booked and no request was sent, and provides a restart action.
The wide paired panels reflow into an orderly narrow sequence without visible clipping. Typography, spacing and the restrained green palette remain coherent through the footer.
limits: Static captures do not verify pointer, keyboard, touch, focus, screen-reader announcements, reset behavior or actual state persistence.

Selected and review captures show flat repair on Thursday at 10:30; confirmation shows brake adjustment on Friday at 14:00. Both states are visible, but continuity of one choice through completion is unverified.
Alternate states are supplied only at narrow width; other widths and zoom are unverified.
No reference pixels were supplied, so reference fidelity cannot be assessed.
